thesis: AMD's Q2 2026 results were a confirmed, company-disclosed beat -- data center revenue grew to over half of total revenue on ~50% YoY growth, positioning AMD as a major AI-infrastructure supplier. The stock has nonetheless pulled back 14.4% over the past 60 days; financial media attribute this to sector-wide risk-off sentiment across semiconductor names (Nvidia and peers also fell 1.5-3% in the same sessions), not any new company-specific deterioration -- a sentiment-driven explanation that discounts the move's fundamental significance even though the underlying growth story is unchanged. No lawsuit, SEC investigation, or governance issue was found for AMD (a search returned only an unrelated company, ADM, plus historical 1990s AMD matters).
invalidation: a Q3 guidance miss or evidence the data-center growth trajectory is slowing

thesis: ATAI Beckley (the merged atai Life Sciences/Beckley Psytech entity) saw a 16.9x volume spike and a 42.9% 60-day price gain, closing within 2.1% of its 52-week high. The catalyst is Q2 2026 earnings showing a narrower net loss year-over-year and continued momentum (90-day return of 78.24%), a confirmed, company-disclosed result -- though Oppenheimer and Deutsche Bank downgraded the stock in mid-August citing valuation, the market's own price/volume reaction since has run counter to that caution, suggesting the earnings improvement is driving sentiment for now. No SEC investigation, restatement, or lawsuit was found; the company's own audit committee statement confirms no restatement review is underway. This is a clinical-stage biopharma, so the several contributing factors (earnings, momentum, analyst skepticism) aren't reduced to one dominant, fully-resolved driver.
invalidation: loss of price/volume momentum, reversal below recent support, or a clinical/regulatory setback

thesis: Dell hit a fresh 52-week high (within 0.9% of it today) after Q2 FY2027 results reported Sept 1, 2026: EPS of $7.04 vs. $4.97 consensus, AI server orders reaching a record $60.9B for the quarter, and an ending backlog of $95B -- a specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst, not a rumor or anticipated event. The strongest counter-case is the stock's own run (+18% in the past month, +20.5% over 60 days) raising pullback/profit-taking risk after such a sharp move -- but the $95B backlog gives multiple quarters of revenue visibility that should support the position regardless of near-term technical profit-taking, since the order book itself (not sentiment) is what re-rated the stock. No lawsuit, SEC investigation, or accounting restatement was found in 2026 (only Dell's historical, fully-settled 2006-2010 SEC accounting matter, well outside the 3-year governance_history window). No unresolved binary catalyst (next earnings is ~3 months out) falls before this position's likely next review.
invalidation: AI server backlog-to-revenue conversion stalls, or Q3 guidance disappoints relative to the newly raised bar

thesis: DYN shares fell roughly 31% intraday on Sept 8, 2026. Yahoo Finance's initial premarket report could not confirm a single catalyst for the drop, but a separate report notes DYN priced an upsized $375M common stock offering around the same window -- a completed dilutive equity raise that is the most likely driver given the timing, even though the two reports don't fully resolve into one confirmed causal story. No lawsuit or governance issue was found beyond a 2025 law-firm investigation into a prior FDA-timeline disclosure that the company's own 10-K says isn't a material legal proceeding. Given the fresh dilution and the unresolved cause of today's drop, this isn't a buy despite the Jan 2027 PDUFA date and upcoming healthcare-conference presentations.
invalidation: the dilutive offering fully absorbed with price stabilization and no further negative catalyst

thesis: Intel fell 12.8% over the past 60 days on a combination of macro pressure (higher bond yields weighing on semiconductor valuations broadly, a sector-wide rather than company-specific driver) and Intel's own completed $20B upsized equity offering (210.5M new shares priced at roughly a 6.5% discount to the prior close) -- a dilutive capital raise. A Delaware Chancery shareholder derivative suit against CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Commerce Secretary Lutnick over an equity-stake-related contract was filed March 5, 2026 and remains pending, but no scheduled hearing, ruling, or trial date within the next ~90 days was found, so it doesn't meet the active_litigation bar; no accounting restatement or executive indictment was found either. Given the fresh dilution layered on top of a macro-driven decline, with no confirmed offsetting catalyst, this isn't a buy.
invalidation: the dilutive offering is fully absorbed, price stabilizes, and the foundry/turnaround narrative resumes

thesis: ServiceTitan fell 18% today (Sept 8, 2026) on its fiscal Q2 report -- a confirmed, already-disclosed, company-specific event, not a rumor. Q2 itself beat estimates (revenue $292.8M vs. $285.9M consensus, adj. EPS $0.40 vs. $0.35 consensus, GTV +17% YoY), the strongest available counter-case to a bearish read -- but Q3 guidance of $285-287M came in below the $287.9M consensus, and full-year guidance was only roughly in line, signaling deceleration. The market's sharp, decisive -18% reaction shows forward guidance is dominating the read over the trailing-quarter beat, which is why this nets out as an avoid despite the beat. No lawsuit, SEC investigation, or restatement was found for ServiceTitan.
invalidation: a subsequent guide-up or evidence the Q3 guidance was conservative rather than an early deceleration signal

thesis: Vertiv pulled back roughly 32% from its May peak after Q2 2026 revenue of $3.274B missed Wall Street's ~$3.38-3.39B estimate -- a confirmed, company-disclosed result. Management attributed the shortfall to temporary supply-chain congestion and timing shifts in large, multi-phase AI data-center deployments rather than softening demand, and raised full-year guidance despite the miss; VRT also announced a $1.45B acquisition of Utility Innovation Holdings to expand AI data-center capabilities. Multiple plaintiffs' law firms have opened investigations into whether Vertiv executives made misleading statements about deployment timing, but none has disclosed a filed complaint with a scheduled hearing, ruling, or trial date, and no restatement or auditor action has been confirmed -- this is solicitation-stage attorney interest, not a confirmed governance failure, so it doesn't rise to a risk flag on its own. The revenue miss (negative) and the raised guidance plus new M&A (positive) are two real, contributing factors without one fully dominant, which is why this reads as medium rather than high conviction.
invalidation: confirmation the Q2 shortfall reflects underlying demand softening rather than timing, or evidence AI data-center capex plans are being pulled back
